chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who made a will, and his heirs were witnesses, and they approved of it, then when the man died, they annulled the will. Is it for them to retract what they acknowledged? He said: It is not for them to do so; the will is binding upon them, if they acknowledged it during his lifetime.
ai.seo_question: Can heirs annul a will they previously approved while the testator was alive?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the binding nature of *ikrar* (acknowledgment) by heirs during the testator's lifetime. This principle underscores that the heirs' consent creates a direct obligation on them, preventing them from later nullifying the bequest as if it were merely a suggestion, thereby protecting the testator's intent and the rights of the beneficiary.
